notes: Supersedes windows-x86_64-2026-07-16.json, which reported a SINGLE run and is therefore not comparable to these medians.
11 consecutive runs, each into a fresh empty directory. read_checksum was identical (1271738) in every run, so the workload is confirmed byte-identical across runs and across the crc32fast change.

Spread is large on this machine: point reads ranged 28.9K-86.9K/s, a 3x span, and the timed phases span 2-4x. This is a power-managed laptop CPU with no pinned clocks; treat the min/max as the honest measurement envelope and the median as the point estimate. Do not quote the max.

The 2026-07-16 artifact's 18.4K writes/s and 117K reads/s were a single observation; the write figure sits below this run's minimum and the read figure above its maximum. That is measurement noise plus a different machine state, NOT a demonstrated regression or improvement from the crc32fast swap.
Includes an fdatasync-equivalent per 100-operation batch. Excludes process startup and release compilation.
For statistically meaningful per-operation numbers prefer the criterion suite: cargo bench --bench engine.
